what_it_does: This work uses a genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) to automatically design optimized FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) architectures. FPGAs are chips whose logic can be reconfigured after manufacture. The algorithm evolves efficient configurations by choosing the right number and mix of general logic blocks, specialized arithmetic units for signal processing (DSPs), and memory blocks (BRAMs) tuned to a specific workload. The goal is to minimize circuit delay and power consumption while keeping performance high.
